description: A focused information pack for malignant mesothelioma, its major anatomic and histologic subtypes, asbestos-related risk, research, treatment studies and life with cancer. It is an information-discovery aid, not medical advice.

synopsis.overview: Mesothelioma is a rare cancer arising from mesothelial tissue, most often the pleura around the lungs, but also the peritoneum, pericardium or tunica vaginalis. Most cases are associated with asbestos exposure, often after a long latency, and the disease is distinct from ordinary lung cancer.
synopsis.manifestations: Symptoms vary by site and may include breathlessness, persistent cough, chest pain, pleural fluid, abdominal pain or swelling, appetite or weight changes, fatigue and nausea. These symptoms have many possible causes, so this information cannot establish a diagnosis.
synopsis.management: Assessment may include history and exposure review, examination, imaging, fluid analysis, biopsy and pathology. Depending on site, stage, cell type, health and goals, specialist teams may discuss surgery, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy, clinical trials and symptom-focused or palliative care.
synopsis.outlook: Mesothelioma is serious and its course varies widely with anatomic site, stage, cell type, biology, response to treatment and general health. Prognosis is individual and should be discussed with the treating cancer team; research and supportive care continue to evolve.

topics.heading: Clinical trials
topics.description: Registered mesothelioma studies, including trials of medicines, immunotherapy, surgery, radiation, procedures, symptom control and supportive care. A listing does not indicate eligibility or recommendation.

termDefinitions.mesothelioma clinical trial: A planned study involving people with mesothelioma that evaluates an intervention or approach under a defined protocol.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma clinical study: A structured investigation involving people with mesothelioma or related cancer questions.
termDefinitions.trial recruitment: The process of identifying and enrolling people who may take part in a clinical study.
termDefinitions.investigational: Being studied and not yet established or approved for the use being investigated.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma trial results: Findings reported after researchers analyse information collected during a mesothelioma clinical study.

topics.heading: Treatment and symptom care
topics.description: Information about surgery, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy, procedures, clinical-trial options and palliative or supportive care for mesothelioma.

termDefinitions.mesothelioma treatment: Medical and supportive care options considered according to mesothelioma site, stage, cell type, health and goals.
termDefinitions.immunotherapy: Treatment that helps the immune system recognise or attack cancer cells.
termDefinitions.chemotherapy: Medicines that kill cancer cells or stop them dividing; the drugs and schedule depend on the cancer and treatment plan.
termDefinitions.pleurectomy and decortication: An operation removing the pleural lining and visible tumour from the chest in selected situations.
termDefinitions.extrapleural pneumonectomy: A major operation removing a lung and associated pleural and nearby tissues in carefully selected cases.
termDefinitions.HIPEC: Heated chemotherapy circulated within the abdomen during or after surgery, used in selected peritoneal cancer settings.
termDefinitions.pleurodesis: A procedure intended to prevent recurrent fluid collecting between the layers around the lung.
termDefinitions.palliative care: Specialist care focused on comfort, symptoms, communication and quality of life at any stage of serious illness.

topics.heading: Mesothelioma research
topics.description: Research into asbestos-related carcinogenesis, tumour biology, biomarkers, pathology, imaging, new medicines, procedures, survivorship and outcomes.

termDefinitions.mesothelioma research: Studies intended to improve understanding, prevention, diagnosis, treatment or support for people affected by mesothelioma.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma biomarker: A measurable feature studied as an indicator of mesothelioma biology, prognosis or response to treatment.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma pathology: The microscopic and molecular examination used to classify tumour tissue.
termDefinitions.mesothelin: A cell-surface protein studied as a mesothelioma biomarker and therapeutic target.
termDefinitions.BAP1 mesothelioma: Mesothelioma research involving BAP1, a gene involved in tumour suppression and DNA repair.
termDefinitions.NF2 mesothelioma: Mesothelioma research involving NF2, a gene associated with tumour biology in some mesotheliomas.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma outcomes: Measures such as symptoms, response, recurrence, survival, quality of life or treatment effects.

topics.heading: Causes, exposure and diagnosis
topics.description: Information about asbestos and other exposures, inherited susceptibility, mesothelioma sites and cell types, imaging, fluid testing, biopsy and pathology.

termDefinitions.asbestos exposure: Breathing or swallowing asbestos fibres, often through occupational, household or environmental contact; exposure history does not by itself diagnose mesothelioma.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma genetics: Study of inherited and tumour genetic factors that may influence susceptibility or tumour behaviour.
termDefinitions.BAP1: A gene involved in cell regulation and DNA repair that can be altered in some tumours and inherited cancer-predisposition syndromes.
termDefinitions.NF2: A gene involved in cell growth regulation that can be altered in some mesotheliomas.
termDefinitions.pleural biopsy: Removal of a small tissue sample from the pleura for laboratory examination.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma diagnosis: The clinical process of identifying mesothelioma using history, imaging, fluid or tissue tests and specialist pathology.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma staging: Assessing how far mesothelioma has spread to help describe disease extent and plan care.
termDefinitions.epithelioid mesothelioma: A mesothelioma cell pattern whose appearance and biology are assessed by specialist pathology.

topics.heading: Living with mesothelioma
topics.description: Daily life with mesothelioma, including breathlessness or pain, fatigue, nutrition, work, practical planning, treatment effects, emotional wellbeing and survivorship.

termDefinitions.living with mesothelioma: Managing everyday life, health and wellbeing while living with mesothelioma or receiving its treatment.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma fatigue: Persistent tiredness that may be related to cancer, treatment, symptoms, sleep or other factors.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma pain: Pain associated with tumour effects, procedures, treatment or other causes that may need specialist assessment.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma nutrition: Food, fluid and nutrition concerns that may arise from cancer, symptoms or treatment.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma survivorship: Ongoing health, follow-up, practical and emotional care after or during mesothelioma treatment.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma quality of life: The physical, emotional, social and practical effects of mesothelioma and its care on daily life.

topics.heading: Caregiving and support
topics.description: Information for family members, care partners and support networks, including appointments, symptom support, communication, practical help, respite and bereavement resources.

termDefinitions.mesothelioma caregiver: A family member, friend or professional who provides practical, personal or emotional support to someone with mesothelioma.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma carer: A person who provides ongoing unpaid or paid support to someone living with mesothelioma.
termDefinitions.family support: Practical and emotional help available to relatives and close supporters of someone affected by mesothelioma.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma support group: People affected by mesothelioma meeting or communicating to exchange information and support.
termDefinitions.care coordination: Organising communication and services among the people and teams involved in someone’s care.
termDefinitions.respite care: Short-term care or support that gives a regular caregiver a temporary break.

topics.heading: Advocacy and access
topics.description: Public awareness, asbestos prevention, occupational health, patient rights, access to specialist cancer care, research funding and condition-focused organisations.

termDefinitions.mesothelioma advocacy: Speaking or acting to improve mesothelioma awareness, rights, services, policy or research.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma awareness: Efforts to improve public understanding of mesothelioma, asbestos risk, symptoms and support.
termDefinitions.asbestos safety: Measures intended to prevent or reduce exposure to asbestos fibres.
termDefinitions.occupational health: Health protection and monitoring related to workplace exposures and conditions.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma education: Information and learning resources about mesothelioma, its effects, care and support.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma funding: Financial support for mesothelioma research, services, advocacy or community programmes.
termDefinitions.mesothelioma rights: Legal and social protections supporting fair treatment and participation for people affected by mesothelioma.
